ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, B is on AC, D is on CE, $AD=BD=BC$, $\angle ACE=25^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $BD=BC$, $\angle ACE=25^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BDC=\angle C=25^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABD=50^\circ$,\\
since $AD=BD$,\\
thus $\angle A=\angle ABD=50^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE=\angle A+\angle C=\boxed{75^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, C, D, E are on the same horizontal straight line, and D is between C and E; A, B, C are on the same slanted line, and B is between A and C; BD and AD are connected in the figure. The problem states that AD=BD=BC, and ∠ACE=25°. Reasoning: Because B is on AC and D is on CE, ray CB and CA are collinear, and ray CD and CE are collinear, so ∠BCD is the same as ∠ACE, ∠BCD=25°. Also because BD=BC, triangle BCD is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, obtaining ∠BDC=∠BCD=25°. Thus ∠CBD=180°−25°−25°=130°. Since A, B, C are collinear, BA and BC are opposite rays, so ∠ABD and ∠CBD are supplementary, ∠ABD=180°−130°=50°. Also because AD=BD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, with base AB, so ∠BAD=∠ABD=50°. In the large triangle ACD, ∠CAD=50°, ∠ACD=25°; and ∠ADE is the exterior angle at point D formed by extending DC to DE, so ∠ADE=∠CAD+∠ACD=50°+25°=75°. Final answer: 75°
